lines.en: label yasuspring4:
scene sky
Somewhere in an undisclosed section of Kumon-mi, a young girl with white hair was caught up in quite the predicament.
She’d been pushed in and out of more medical facilities than most would be able to stomach lately. But for her, this wasn’t much of a bother at all.
She’d become somewhat desensitized to it over the years. And while the rate at which she encountered them had screeched to a halt following her abandonment, those acquired behaviors still lingered.
Where to write your name. How much pressure to apply to the paper with the tips of different types of pens. What certain questions mean. What other ones don’t. Who to give the clipboard back to.
And while all of this could be easily ascertained by someone with a sound mind, it was something that people like her needed to figure out as time went by.
And oh, how it did. Oh, how the days passed by — once loud, now quiet. But becoming louder the closer she came to a happier medium despite being one herself.
“If any of that’s even true,” she’d think — acknowledging the narration in a subdued and suppressed effort to ignore the whispers of the world. Another learned behavior.
Or was it a gift?
scene yasutaco1

Whatever the case, years of experience had taught her that showing her true colors amounted to little in a world so centered around the colorblind. She was a misfit. An outlier. A shadow, if you will.
But also a bit of a chameleon, you see. For she was and always would be herself, even when it didn’t seem like it. Those parts of her existence she abhorred and feared were still part of her.
And learning how to control them was but one of many things that she unfortunately never learned between all of the clipboards and empty spaces in which she could scribe her insignificance.
Maybe that would end today, though?
Maybe tomorrow will come and she’ll be able to wake up less worried about being the character she needs to be and can focus instead on being more of a...normal girl.
One who likes strawberry daifuku and karaoke. One who enjoys those violent comics her newest friend reads, but must pretend she doesn’t because of a nagging, constant assertion that she shouldn’t.

One who can live a normal life beside everyone else — where they won’t see her falsely blending in with her surroundings and, instead, come to accept her as an active participant in their shared existence.
Or maybe it wouldn’t — and she’d live tomorrow as a ghost as well.
: This is entirely unacceptable! Do you have any idea who I am?!
Thankfully, there was someone who’d accept her regardless of who she was on any given day. And she would never stop being grateful for that.
: Yes, Miss Tsukioka. You have mentioned it many times now. But I’m afraid that policy is policy and that we can only allow members of Miss Yasui’s family to remain in the room for her consultation.
: I am her family! And I implore- no, I command you to take a closer look at the hanko on her file and see with your own, damnable eyes that it belongs to who, doctor?!

: The Tsukioka family. I am well aware of your family’s seal, Miss Tsukioka. But despite your mother’s legal guardianship of her, the fact remains that our policy is specific to blood relatives. And Miss Yasui-
scene yasutaco2

: TO HELL WITH YOUR POLICY! You think I don’t know that this institution is propped up on donations from the Tsukioka Foundation?! Do you have any idea how quickly I could pull those donations, doctor?!
: That...surely, you wouldn’t. Such a thing would leave hundreds of patients without proper medical care and-
: THEN WE’D TAKE THEM ELSEWHERE, YOU INCOMPETENT BUFFOON! Unlike you, I’m not willing to leave those in need of help...in need of help!
: Is everything okay, Touka? You seem a little angry today.
: NO! Everything is not okay! This heathen won’t let me remain in the room with you! When I specifically informed the hospital staff that I must!
: I can do it alone if it causes a problem. You don’t need to-
: I AM STAYING AND THAT IS FINAL! DO YOU UNDERSTAND, DOCTOR?! Or do I need to call my father and put an end to this FARCE disguised as a hospital once and for all?!
: Hah...fine. You win. You can stay. Just...take a seat in the corner and please don’t interfere.
scene yasutaco3
: Oh, splendid! Thank you very much for reconsidering. I sincerely apologize for any inappropriate language I may have used just now.
: You’re kind of scary when you get mad, Touka...I didn’t know someone as pretty and nice as you could say things like that.
: I excel at getting things done, Yasu. Doctor.
: Yes, yes. You’re very threatening. Now, if you could please take a seat, I’d like to see the actual patient now.
scene black
: Come, Yasu. Take a seat on the bed and let me double check your registration form. I’ll be right over here if you need me, okay?
: Okay! Thank you, Touka. And hello, doctor. I hope I will not be a burden.
: I’m sure you won’t be, Miss Yasui.
: Now, tell me — are you still hearing these “voices” I've been informed of?
scene yasutaco4
: Oh, thank heavens. For a moment, I was worried we were going to strike out at that hospital as well. There are only so many left in this city propped up by my family’s coffers.
: I wonder if this is how the common man feels finding a medical provider?
: You were...really scary back there, Touka.
scene yasutaco5
: You need to be scary in order to get anything done sometimes, Yasu. That was one of the first lessons I ever learned from my mother.
: The only issue now is making sure that things continue to go well as there is always a chance that the effects of your new medication may begin to wear off.
: The follow-up...went well, though...didn’t it? Did I do a good job?
scene yasutaco6
: Oh, yes. Exemplary, even. You followed all of my directions perfectly. How did you feel it went, though? Does this new doctor make you feel uncomfortable at all?
scene yasutaco7
: He seems nice...same as the last one I saw there...
: They don’t make me feel strange when I tell them about the things I’ve heard. And the rooms aren’t very cold.
: When I was a smaller and even less significant worm, many of the places I visited-
scene yasutaco8
: Don’t...bring up those days, please. It pains me hearing about what you went through.
: Oh...I’m sorry, Touka. I must have forgotten.
: There’s no need to apologize. I’m satisfied enough just knowing that such a thing won’t be happening to anyone else in the future ever again.
: You can’t prevent misery from seeping into every minute aspect of our unfortunate lives, though. Tragedy will continue to befall us no matter what you do.
scene yasutaco9
: True. But I can dispose of those who make such a feat more difficult to accomplish. And feel very little remorse in the process!
scene yasutaco10
: Now! Who wants tacos?!
: What’s a taco?
: You’ll soon find out, Yasu!
: Oh, if it isn’t my favorite customer.
scene yasutaco11
: Hello again, Touka Man.
: Hello again, Taco Tsukioka. Same order as always, I assume?
: If you could prepare three of your best tacos for my good friend here as well, it would be greatly appreciated. We’re currently celebrating her road to mental recovery.
: That’s great. Would you like me to sing her a song?
: That would be fantastic, actually! Thank you.
: Of course. Ahem.
: Somebody once told me the world is gonna roll me-
: Okay, that’s enough. Thank you.
: Of course. I’ll get to work on your tacos now.
scene yasutaco12
: Wow, Touka. Everyone really does love you. You’re totally different from a slug like me.
: Another lesson I learned from my mother is that anyone will like you if you give them enough money. And I make it a habit to stop by this stand at least once per week.
: Really? How come I’ve never heard of this place?

: I was saving it for a special occasion, of course. And what’s more special than finding the perfect balance of pills for you to take to still hear things, but not so many things that it becomes an issue?
: My birthday maybe?
: Yes, I suppose that is important as well.
scene black
: Come! Let’s have a seat and await our mediocre Mexican street food together!
scene yasutaco13
It was just as Touka said.
Not the mediocre Mexican street food part. I’m a disembodied voice and even I know that tacos are the shit. I’m referring specifically to that thing about “balance.”

Because, while Touka and her mother initially believed that it would be healthiest to sever Yasu’s connection to “whatever it is she’s connected to,” they changed their minds nearly the minute they saw the results.
As it turns out, using pills to effectively lobotomize someone takes away a lot of what made you love them in the first place. And Yasu really was loved. By both of the family’s matriarchs.
Which is precisely why she was taken in as one of them. But while she may never be a true Tsukioka in terms of blood, she can leech off their benefits and connections and remain close.
It was perfect, yet unusual for someone like her who had never felt connected to anything outside of a strange system of beliefs practically embedded into her at birth.
Could such contrasting concepts find a way to coexist, though? That was the question she had to ask herself now.
Was there another sort of balance that could be found — halfway between normal and paranormal?
Something that would allow her to nurture the love she had for her Father, while still going home to a pair of unconnected mothers she trusted even when she was being told that she couldn’t.
She would not find the answer inside of a taco — she would find it in time.
scene yasutaco14
: Ahh...
But that doesn’t mean she wouldn’t try to find it in a taco anyway.
: Dear lord, Yasu. What are you doing?
scene yasutaco15
: AhhIdnnhhtwrng?
: Never speak with your mouth full. Or...while licking something. Put your tongue away and try again.
scene yasutaco16
: Am I doing it wrong?...
: Completely wrong. You’re meant to bite into the taco and consume the contents.
scene yasutaco17
: Like how He Who Leaves the Light On consumes the unborn souls of all of His potential children as a means of saving them from the unseen?
: Sure. If that’s what gets you to stop licking the taco.
scene yasutaco18
: I understand now!
: Great!
scene yasutaco19
: But I’m not very hungry...
: Not so great!
: Maybe I’m just too worried to eat though?...
scene yasutaco20
: Worried about what, exactly? Is there some sort of side effect from your new medication that you neglected to mention? We can still go back to the hospital. They’re open twenty four hours a-
: There’s no side effect, Touka...
: I’m just worried you’ll stop liking me.
scene yasutaco21
: ...What?
: You don’t want me to hear anything. It’s why you tried to fix me in the first place.
: So it confuses me that you’re happy now that I can hear again.
: I feel like I’ve failed you. I’ve failed God. I’ve failed myself.
: I really am just a worm.
scene yasutaco22
: You have not failed anyone. We simply made a mistake in thinking we knew what was best for you.
: But we understand how important these...voices are to your identity now. We don’t want to deprive you of them.
: You won’t be scared of me if they make me act strange again? You won’t be annoyed?
: I won’t be scared, Yasu.
: But you’ll be annoyed?
scene yasutaco23
: I am a bucket of discarded entrails...
: I only kid, of course! Your...eccentricity may annoy some. But it’s become just one more way of life for me. I will accept you regardless of who you are...what you see...what you hear.
scene yasutaco24
: Thank you...but unfortunately, I don’t feel entirely like myself again yet.
: I can hear again...but only a little bit. Not like it was before.
: It’s like when the radio is on, but the volume is turned to the lowest level and you can only make out the words if you try really hard and everything else goes quiet.
: When have you ever encountered a radio?
: There was one in the alley I used to sleep in, but the reception was very bad so I just listened to the static. I could still make out what words were supposed to be there, though.
: I see! So we just need to find a way to turn the volume up then, don’t we?
scene yasutaco25
: But wouldn’t turning the volume up defeat the purpose of going to the doctor in the first place?...
scene yasutaco26
: Not if it’s only temporary.
: Temporary?...
: Temporary. The entire idea behind medicating you at all was to make it easier for you to assimilate and blend in with the outside world. But...perhaps in a controlled environment...
: Hearing everything wouldn’t be as harmful as we think?
: So I...can stop taking the medicine at home?
scene yasutaco27
: Well, your doctors have advised that you shouldn’t stop taking it — especially not abruptly as it could have some unforeseen effects on your mental health...
: But maybe there’s a way to turn the volume up without depriving you of the medication? Do you have any ideas? Would going to the cathedral help, perhaps?
scene yasutaco28
: Or maybe there are certain words or triggers we could use to-
: Being around...Sensei...helps sometimes...
scene yasutaco29
: Sensei?
: The voices are...louder when he’s around...
: But it’s been a long time since I’ve heard them, so...
: There’s a chance his light has died...and he’s been abandoned by He who would never abandon anyone.
: But if “He who would never abandon anyone” abandoned someone-
: You just don’t get it.
: No...I suppose I do not.
scene yasutaco30
: But that doesn’t mean I’m not opposed to running a bit of a test.
: A test?...But only He can test me for it is He who judges my-
: Yes, yes. But we’re testing your ability to hear Him right now — which means all we must do is get into contact with Sensei and see if he has any effect on your new mix of anti-psychotic formulas.
: If he doesn’t, will you put me out of misery and drive a rusty stake through my heart so I can finally feel the taste of the outer plane and better commune with those who have vanished?
: Deal!
scene yasutaco31
: Yay! Ascension!
: I’ll give him a call right now, okay?
